display_name.description: A human-readable display name for the custom module.
display_name.rationale: Display names are for usability only and do not impact security.

type.description: The immutable type of Event Threat Detection module. Determines what kind of threat the module detects.
type.rationale: Using a valid detection type (e.g., CONFIGURABLE_BAD_IP) ensures the module functions correctly. Invalid types prevent proper detection.

organization.description: The numerical ID of the parent organization where the module is deployed.
organization.rationale: This ID determines scope but does not directly affect detection or security posture.

config.description: Configuration details for the custom module. Includes metadata such as severity, description, recommendation, and the IPs to detect.
config.rationale: The configuration defines the detection logic. Incorrect or empty values will result in incomplete or ineffective threat detection.
config.compliant: { "metadata": { "severity": "LOW", "description": "Flagged by Forcepoint as malicious", "recommendation": "Contact the owner of the relevant project." }, "ips": ["192.0.2.1", "192.0.2.0/24"] }

enablement_state.description: Specifies whether the custom module is enabled or disabled. Must be ENABLED for detection to occur.
enablement_state.rationale: If disabled, the module will not detect threats, creating monitoring gaps.
